\title{Physical-Reward Policy Optimization for Accelerator RTL}

\author{Mohamed~Amine~Hallam, Kuo-Kun~Tseng, and Wenjie~Pei%
\thanks{Mohamed Amine Hallam, Kuo-Kun Tseng, and Wenjie Pei are with the
School of Computer Science and Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology
(e-mail: \texttt{25sf51027@stu.hit.edu.cn}; \texttt{ykktseng@hit.edu.cn};
\texttt{wenjiecoder@outlook.com}).}%
}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We investigate whether training with a learned physical reward improves the
RTL that a policy generates at a fixed sampling budget. During training, an
executable oracle screens candidate behavior and gates the physical reward.
Independent post-route implementation then evaluates the trained
policy, preserving the frequency of each sampled candidate and assigning zero
to functional and implementation failures. On a separately frozen
\studyclaim{StudyTwoDesignCount}-design split, two policies initialized from the
same supervised fine-tuned (SFT) checkpoint and trained with a canonical-feature
random-forest (RF) reward increase failure-penalized timing-derived maximum frequency from
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallSftPenalized} to
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfPenalized}~MHz. The paired gain is
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfSftGain}~MHz with a
\studyclaim{StudyTwoBootstrapConfidence}\% design-bootstrap interval of
[\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfSftCiLow},
\studyclaim{StudyTwoOverallRfSftCiHigh}]~MHz. Both RF seeds improve, and matched
controls show that the gain cannot be explained by functional yield alone.
The RF reward also outperforms the original multilayer-perceptron reward
package. A separate setup-closure extension reproduces the positive RF and
negative correctness-only effects in two additional seeds per arm, while an
earlier Qwen-Coder experiment improves all \claim{QwenDesignCount} tested
designs. Structural analysis and paired board measurements help explain these
gains, which accompany higher resource costs, weak median-filter outcomes,
and a small regression on general RTL tasks. The findings support physical
reward training within the studied accelerator domain and show why its
evaluation must account for failures and use independent physical measurements.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
FPGA physical design, hardware-aware optimization, large language models,
reinforcement learning, reward-model reliability, RTL generation
\end{IEEEkeywords}
